This bead asks for the Go type additions described in the amended
CONTRACT-003 spec (Role + CorrelationID on ExecuteRequest/RouteRequest,
Power on ServiceRoutingActual, typed validators, RoutingActual.Power
populated at dispatch, MetadataKeyCollision warning).

All five acceptance criteria are already implemented and tested by prior
work on this branch:

  - 8c0cca7 feat(contract): add Role + CorrelationID + Power to
    CONTRACT-003 [agent-3bb96bf5]
  - 404684a docs(contract): finalize CONTRACT-003 spec amendments
    [agent-bc214918]

Concrete AC evidence:

  AC1 — Types updated.
    * service.go:593 ServiceExecuteRequest.Role / CorrelationID
    * service.go:356 RouteRequest.Role / CorrelationID
    * service.go:428 RouteDecision.Power
    * service_events.go:258 ServiceRoutingActual.Power

  AC2 — Validators reject invalid Role / CorrelationID with typed
        errors.
    * role_correlation.go RoleNormalizationError /
      CorrelationIDNormalizationError, ValidateRole / ValidateCorrelationID.
    * Wired into Execute (service_execute.go) and ResolveRoute
      (service_routing.go) before dispatch.
    * Covered by service_role_correlation_test.go
      (TestRoleAndCorrelationID_InvalidValuesRejectedPreDispatch +
      TestValidateRoleAndCorrelationID).

  AC3 — RoutingActual.Power populated correctly across all harnesses.
    * Single funnel point in service_execute.go finalizeAndEmit
      (line 1419) stamps Power = catalogPowerForModel(...) onto every
      terminal RoutingActual that lacked one.
    * Pre-decision Power is set in runExecute (service_execute.go:223)
      via the same projection.
    * Models not in the catalog (e.g. the virtual harness used in
      tests) report Power = 0 per the contract's documented
      "unknown / exact-pin-only" semantics.

  AC4 — Collision warning event fires under integration test.
    * service_execute.go finalizeAndEmit appends a
      ServiceFinalWarning{Code: "metadata_key_collision"} to the final
      event's Warnings when the caller's Metadata duplicates a reserved
      key (role / correlation_id) and the top-level field overrode it.
    * Asserted by
      TestRoleAndCorrelationID_TopLevelWinsOnMetadataCollisionWithWarning
      in service_role_correlation_test.go.

  AC5 — Existing tests still pass.
    * `go build ./...` clean.
    * `go vet ./...` clean.
    * `go test -count=1 -timeout 300s ./...` — all packages OK
      (verified in this worktree at base 3257b39).

6. TestRoutingQualityMetricsClassBreakdown verifies: feeding override events with mixed prompt_features and axes produces the expected pivot, including outcome aggregation (success/stalled/failed counts per bucket).

New metrics computed from override and rejected_override events emitted by bead 1 (agent-9fc2633c):
- auto_acceptance_rate = no-override requests / total requests (windowed)
- override_disagreement_rate = (overrides where pin != auto on at least one overridden axis) / overrides. Coincidental-agreement overrides are in the denominator but not the numerator.
- override_class_breakdown = pivot of (prompt_features bucket, axis_overridden, match_per_axis) -> count + outcome aggregates.

- Existing per-(provider, model) success-rate field on RouteStatusReport gets renamed or relabeled as 'provider reliability' / ProviderReliabilityRate. Stays mechanically the same.

- UsageReport gains a RoutingQuality summary section (totals over the report window).

- service_routestatus_test.go and usage_report_test.go (metric correctness)

The agent library sends an Anthropic-specific `thinking` field in OpenAI-compatible request bodies to non-Anthropic providers (lmstudio, omlx, openrouter, ollama). Providers that accept and parse the request then silently terminate their SSE stream after the first delta frame when their generation pipeline encounters the unknown field. Downstream consumers see `unexpected end of JSON input`.

This bug was classified via wire capture using the new AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE=1 flag (this repo's agent-941e7e42, landed in v0.3.12). Evidence was gathered from DocumentDrivenDX/ddx ddx-6a5dfe35.

## Wire evidence (v0.3.12, 2026-04-18)

```
POST http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions
Content-Type: application/json
Body includes:
  "stream":true,
  "stream_options":{"include_usage":true},
  "thinking":{"budget_tokens":8192,"type":"enabled"},
  "tools":[... 6 tools ...],
  "model":"Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit"
```

Response:
- HTTP 200
- Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
- Body captured: 186 bytes total
  - Frame 1: `: keep-alive\n\n` (SSE keepalive)
  - Frame 2: valid `data: {..."delta":{"role":"assistant"}}\n\n` (assistant role start)
  - Then: stream terminates. No `data: [DONE]`. No error frame. Just EOF.

`thinking` is Anthropic's extended-thinking API. It is NOT in the OpenAI chat-completions schema. vidar-omlx (OpenAI-compatible, no Anthropic semantics) has no handler for it and its generation pipeline fails silently mid-stream.

Reproduced on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit AND Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit — model-independent. Reproduced across two projects (ddx repo + agent repo) — project-independent. Reproduced on v0.3.11 and v0.3.12 — both versions exhibit the bug.

## Root cause

The openai-compat provider's request-serialization path does not gate flavor-specific fields. `thinking` is serialized into the wire body unconditionally when the caller has passed the equivalent Anthropic-style configuration (via preset or CLI flag). Since v0.3.12 now has Provider.DetectedFlavor() (agent-92f0f324), the library has the information it needs to gate this — it just doesn't use it in the serializer.

## Fix direction

In the openai-compat provider's Chat/ChatStream request builder:

1. Before writing the request body, check `p.DetectedFlavor()`.
2. If the flavor is NOT one that supports Anthropic thinking semantics (i.e., NOT `anthropic-passthrough` or similar — in practice all current openai-compat flavors: lmstudio, omlx, openrouter, ollama, plus `openai-native`), omit the `thinking` field from the serialized JSON.
3. Emit a debug log (at Trace level or via AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE when that flag is on) noting that `thinking` was stripped for flavor X. Operators should see this when diagnosing 'why isn't my local model using thinking'.

The anthropic provider package continues to include the field in its own serializer (no change there).

Long term, consider a broader per-flavor field allowlist/denylist in the openai-compat serializer — `thinking` is probably not the only Anthropic-specific field that leaks. Audit the request builder for other non-portable fields.

## Alternative (less preferred)

Reject at config-load: if Config passes `thinking` config AND any provider in the same config has a non-Anthropic DetectedFlavor, emit a startup warning. Does not help when providers are added at runtime and does not handle the case where a single agent run targets multiple providers with different flavors in the same session.

Stripping at serialization is cleaner.

## Other non-portable fields likely to have the same issue

These are candidates for the same per-flavor gate:
- `metadata` with Anthropic-specific keys
- `system` as a top-level field vs in messages array (OpenAI uses messages[].role=system; some providers may tolerate both, some may not)
- `anthropic_version` or similar API-version fields
- Extended-thinking budget controls beyond `thinking`

Audit as part of the fix; file follow-up beads if other fields exhibit the same symptom.

DDx consumer goal G3: "the selected provider should be the 'best' that meets whatever the requirements are — available, with quota available, **and lowest cost**." Today the routing engine has no cost dimension on `ProviderEntry`; scoring uses only quota + cooldown + perf + locality. When two providers serve the same model with different prices, the engine picks by name or score, not cost.

## Scope

### Data model

Add to `internal/routing.ProviderEntry`:

- `CostUSDPer1kTokens float64` — nil/zero if unknown.
- `CostSource string` — `"catalog" | "subscription" | "unknown" | "user-config"`. Surfaces in decision trace so operators know where the number came from.

Populate at `buildRoutingInputs` time:

- **Endpoint providers (openrouter, lmstudio, omlx, ollama, minimax, qwen, zai, openai):** look up in the existing model catalog (`internal/modelcatalog`) by resolved model ID. When the catalog has a price, use it. When absent, leave zero + `CostSource: "unknown"`.
- **Subscription harnesses (claude, codex, gemini):** compute an **effective** cost as a function of quota utilization:
  - At 0-70% quota used: effective cost = 0 (fixed-cost subscription, near-zero marginal).
  - At 70-90%: effective cost = low (encourage spreading load).
  - At 90-100%: effective cost = high (near-quota demotion).
  - Exact numbers in the bead acceptance; tunable via `ServiceOptions`.
  - `CostSource: "subscription"`.
- **`agent` harness (local via endpoints):** cost = electricity estimate from config (off by default — `CostSource: "unknown"` when not configured). Operators who want to model local cost set `ServiceOptions.LocalCostUSDPer1kTokens`.

### Scoring changes

`internal/routing/score.go`: add cost as a tiebreak dimension **after** eligibility, quota OK, and base score. Order becomes:
1. Eligible
2. Quota OK / healthy
3. Base score (profile policy, cooldowns, perf bias) — unchanged
4. **Cost (lower is better)** — new
5. Locality (local cost-class preferred)
6. Name

For unknown-cost providers (`CostSource: "unknown"`): treat as **neutral** in the cost tiebreak — neither preferred nor demoted, so they don't starve known-cost providers but aren't penalized into last place.

### Unknown-cost policy

A documented rule: when all viable candidates have `CostSource: "unknown"`, the cost tiebreak is skipped and locality/name decide. Test covers this.

## Subscription-quota pricing curve

Default curve (tunable):
- 0-70% used: effective $/1k tokens = 0
- 70-80%: 0.1× the pay-per-token rate for the equivalent model
- 80-90%: 0.3× pay-per-token
- 90-100%: 1.2× pay-per-token (demote below pay-per-token so routing drains the subscription gracefully)","events":[{"actor":"ddx","body":"{"resolved_provider":"codex","resolved_model":"gpt-5.4","fallback_chain":[]}","created_at":"2026-04-22T22:28:03.514071808Z","kind":"routing","source":"ddx agent execute-bead","summary":"provider=codex model=gpt-5.4"},{"actor":"ddx","body":"{"attempt_id":"20260422T221752-b80b77f9","harness":"codex","model":"gpt-5.4","input_tokens":6111437,"output_tokens":25247,"total_tokens":6136684,"cost_usd":0,"duration_ms":611177,"exit_code":0}","created_at":"2026-04-22T22:28:03.556977615Z","kind":"cost","source":"ddx agent execute-bead","summary":"tokens=6136684 model=gpt-5.4"},{"actor":"ddx","body":"{"escalation_count":0,"fallback_chain":[],"final_tier":"","requested_profile":"","requested_tier":"","resolved_model":"gpt-5.4","resolved_provider":"codex","resolved_tier":""}","created_at":"2026-04-22T22:29:23.411075797Z","kind":"routing","source":"ddx agent execute-loop","summary":"provider=codex model=gpt-5.4"},{"actor":"ddx","body":"REQUEST_CHANGES

DDx and other upstream consumers need `--profile default`, `--profile local`, `--profile standard` to be first-class profiles with documented, predictable rules. Today the engine treats `default` as an unnamed fall-through via `providerPreferenceForProfile(service_routing.go:368-377)` — the default case returns `ProviderPreferenceLocalFirst` — but there is no explicit catalog entry defining the profile's contract. `local` is not mapped at all (only `offline`/`air-gapped` map to `LocalOnly`). `standard` is unmapped and falls through identically to `default`.

A DDx consumer materializing `Profile: "default"` against an endpoint-only config gets unpredictable fallthrough behavior depending on which harnesses happen to be available. The profile catalog must define the contract.

## Scope

Add first-class profile entries in `internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` for:

- `default` — balanced, prefer local endpoints when available, fall back to subscription harnesses, avoid pay-per-token unless specified. `ProviderPreferenceLocalFirst`.
- `local` — **hard** local-only constraint (same as `offline`). If no local-endpoint candidate is eligible, return typed error. `ProviderPreferenceLocalOnly`.
- `standard` — cost-balanced tier; prefer standard-capability endpoints. `ProviderPreferenceLocalFirst` but with cost-ceiling bias.

Retain existing `cheap`, `smart`, `fast`, `code-high`, `offline`, `air-gapped` entries unchanged.

Move the `providerPreferenceForProfile` decision out of hardcoded `service_routing.go` into the catalog so profile-to-preference mapping is data, not code.

## Override precedence (DOC2)

Publish the rule: **explicit pin wins within profile constraint; pin-violates-profile is a typed error, not a silent substitution.**

Worked examples included in docs:
- `--profile local --harness claude` → if claude is non-local (subscription harness), upstream returns `ErrProfilePinConflict` naming which side is incompatible.
- `--profile default --model gpt-5.4` → profile supplies preferences; explicit model overrides tier selection within those preferences.

disposition explicit and on-record.

What the bead asks for
----------------------

The acceptance offers three alternatives, any one of which closes
the bead:

  (a) routing/catalog change preventing Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit from
      being auto-selected for multi-file refactor work,
  (b) a fix to whatever in the agent's loop is causing
      false-positive tool-call-repeat detection,
  (c) explicit confirmation in the catalog notes that this model
      isn't suitable for agentic refactor work,

plus: "the seven beads cited in the description have a documented
disposition (closed via different harness, deferred, or used as
fixtures)."

Why none of (a)/(b)/(c) is the right action right now
-----------------------------------------------------

(a) Catalog/routing is not the lever for this model. The static
    catalog at internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml registers
    qwen3.5-27b and qwen3.5-7b but not Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit. The
    omlx provider (internal/provider/omlx/omlx.go) discovers MLX
    models dynamically from the local server's /v1/models/status
    endpoint at request time — they are never registered statically
    in the agent catalog. Adding a "tier=unsuitable" or capability
    constraint to a static entry would not affect dispatch for a
    model that the catalog has no row for. Auto-selection of MLX
    models is governed by the local server's model listing and by
    ddx-side tier policy, not by anything in this repo.

(b) The bead's own notes explicitly defer the tool-loop-detection
    angle: "The one actionable angle that lives here — 'is tool-loop
    detection too eager?' — is a separate small bead that can be
    filed if/when investigation is justified by other models also
    tripping the guard." That justification has not appeared (no
    other harness/model is tripping ErrToolCallLoop). For when a
    follow-up bead is filed, the relevant code is:

      internal/core/loop.go:703-719  — fingerprint + 3-strike abort
      internal/core/errors.go:20-22  — ErrToolCallLoop
      toolCallLoopLimit              — currently 3 consecutive
                                       identical tool-call sets

    Any future investigation should distinguish (i) legitimate
    repetition the guard wrongly aborts, from (ii) genuine model
    failure modes the guard correctly catches. Without that
    distinction, loosening the limit risks masking real capability
    failures with longer runs and higher token spend (the bead
    already cites a 2.65M-input-token 41-minute attempt).

(c) Adding "NOT GOOD AT: multi-file refactor" notes to the catalog
    requires (i) extending the catalog schema (models.yaml has no
    notes/capabilities free-text field today) and its loader, and
    (ii) targeting a row that doesn't exist for the MLX 8bit
    variant. Both are out of proportion to a P4 capability-of-
    third-party-quantized-weights observation that the bead's own
    notes describe as "not a routing/discovery/context-window/
    prompt-size bug in this repo."

Seven cited beads
-----------------

The seven beads referenced in the description
(ddx-0a33bc5f, ddx-915240dd, ddx-9ce6842a, ddx-dd7fce7e,
ddx-0b382233, ddx-d1d7ca17, ddx-ee2cd434) live in
/Users/erik/Projects/ddx/.ddx/beads.jsonl, a different workspace.
This worktree cannot modify their disposition. Their natural
disposition is the standard execute-loop fallback: re-attempt with
a higher-tier harness (claude/opus, gemini-pro, gpt-5.4) on the
next claim, which the queue already does for repeatedly-failed
beads via adaptive min-tier — exactly the policy the bead's
"keep with known low success rate" suggestion endorses.

What a follow-up attempt would need
-----------------------------------

This bead is most useful left open at P4 as a tracking record,
exactly as the notes prescribe. It should only be reopened with
code intent if one of the following occurs:

  - A second, unrelated harness/model combination starts tripping
    ErrToolCallLoop on legitimate work. That justifies the
    "is tool-loop detection too eager?" follow-up bead and the
    accompanying loop.go investigation.
  - The agent catalog gains a capability-constraint schema (e.g.
    via ADR), at which point this bead becomes a concrete first
    candidate for "NOT GOOD AT: multi-file refactor" annotation —
    but only after the omlx provider is changed to consult that
    metadata for dynamically-discovered MLX models, since the
    static catalog rows alone cannot describe them.
  - A reproducer is built that distinguishes false-positive from
    true-positive tool-loop aborts on Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit
    specifically, with a concrete proposal to either raise
    toolCallLoopLimit, change the fingerprint definition, or add a
    backoff window. Today the failure mode (model gets stuck
    repeating one tool call) is consistent with a true-positive
    capability-ceiling abort, not a false-positive guard bug.

No code changes were made in this worktree.

Status: no commit produced this attempt.

What is done
- Mapped the current split:
  - cmd/agent/main.go:605-800 — resolveProviderForRun → buildRouteSelection → buildSmartRoutePlan → newRouteProvider. The constructed route provider (`p`) is then DISCARDED at main.go:167 (assigned to `_`). Only the `selection` and `pc` are used downstream.
  - cmd/agent/main.go:439-489 — buildServiceExecuteRequest converts selection.RouteCandidates into req.PreResolved with Harness="agent", Provider/Model from candidate[0].
  - cmd/agent/routing_provider.go — full routeProvider failover wrapper (Chat/ChatStream + health-state I/O). The Chat/ChatStream methods are now unreachable at runtime (the constructed instance is discarded); only the helpers (routeAttemptOrder, healthyCandidateIndexes, loadRouteHealthState, saveRouteHealthState, routeHealthCooldown) are still consumed by routing_smart.go for the route-status display path and by cmdRouteStatus.
  - service_execute.go:837-913 — serviceRouteProvider already owns chat-time failover over decision.Candidates and stamps Attempt.ProviderName / Attempt.Route / Response.Attempt for routing_actual.
  - service_routing.go:26-65 — ResolveRoute delegates to internal/routing.Resolve. It does NOT currently consult ServiceConfig.ModelRouteConfig (it iterates ServiceConfig.ProviderNames() into HarnessEntry.Providers without filtering by configured route candidate lists).

What is blocking
- The bead requires the SERVICE to be the only owner of route resolution + failover for native, including respecting user-configured `model_routes` (strategy + ordered candidates). Today the routing engine treats model_routes as invisible: it skips providers whose /v1/models probe fails (probeEndpointDiscoveredIDs returns false), so the engine's Decision.Candidates does not include "dead-but-explicitly-configured" providers.
- Existing CLI integration tests load-bear on the explicit ordering:
  - TestCLI_ModelRouteFailoverOnAvailabilityError (cmd/agent/routing_cli_test.go:288): expects attempted_providers=[bragi, openrouter] and failover_count=1 when bragi is dead and a model_route lists [bragi, openrouter].
  - TestCLI_ModelRouteDoesNotFailoverOnDeterministic400 (cmd/agent/routing_cli_test.go:351): expects bragi attempted (and only bragi) on a 400; openrouter never reached.
  Without the CLI synthesizing PreResolved from model_routes, the engine would currently strip bragi from the candidate list (the /v1/models probe returns 503), and the test's first-attempted-provider expectation would fail.
- Therefore the refactor requires:
  1. Service-side: in ResolveRoute (or in resolveExecuteRouteWithEngine), when a request's Model matches a configured ServiceConfig.ModelRouteConfig with strategy ordered-failover or priority-round-robin, bypass the routing engine and emit a RouteDecision whose Candidates are the explicit configured list in strategy order. Smart strategy should still fall through to internal/routing.Resolve.
  2. CLI: stop populating selection.RouteCandidates and stop synthesizing PreResolved in buildServiceExecuteRequest; instead pass intent fields (Model/ModelRef/Provider/Harness) verbatim. The CLI must still resolve a representative concrete model for compactionContextWindow/maxTokens lookup OR move that resolution into the service.
  3. Delete cmd/agent execution-path code (routeProvider Chat/ChatStream/buildCandidate/recordAttempt/markCandidateFailure/RoutingReport, newRouteProvider, withModelOverride, routeError, shouldFailover) and update cmd/agent/route_provider_test.go and the routeProvider parts of cmd/agent/routing_internal_test.go. Helpers used by routing_smart.go (route-status display) must remain.
  4. Verify TestCLI_ModelRoute*, TestExecuteEndpointFirstRouting* (in service_http_provider_test.go), TestResolveRoute*, TestRouteStatus*, and TestBuildServiceExecuteRequestPreservesNativeLoopSettings still pass; the last one explicitly asserts serviceReq.PreResolved == nil, which is consistent with the bead's direction.

Why no commit this pass
- The refactor crosses CLI ↔ service ↔ routing engine boundaries and requires a new model_routes-aware short-circuit inside service_routing.go. Doing this safely without regressing the CLI integration tests above requires careful staged changes (with each layer's tests run between steps). Attempting to land it in a single short pass risks committing red code, which is worse than re-queuing per the bead instructions.

What a follow-up attempt would need
- Add a model_routes-aware path in service_routing.go::ResolveRoute (or a new helper invoked from resolveExecuteRouteWithEngine) that, when ServiceConfig.ModelRouteConfig(req.Model).Candidates is non-empty AND strategy is "ordered-failover" or "priority-round-robin", returns a RouteDecision built directly from the configured list (Harness=agent, Candidates in strategy order, Provider/Model from the first). For strategy "" or "smart", continue through routing.Resolve (which already produces a ranked Candidates list that serviceRouteProvider iterates).
- Strip selection.RouteCandidates and the PreResolved synthesis block in cmd/agent/main.go (lines 472-487 and the producing branch in buildRouteSelection at lines 789-798). Have buildServiceExecuteRequest only emit intent fields. Resolve representative model/context-window for compaction either via a pre-Execute call to svc.ResolveRoute or by moving compaction-config derivation into service_execute.go.
- Delete cmd/agent/routing_provider.go's Chat/ChatStream path and the routeProvider type entirely; keep route-health helpers used by routing_smart.go. Trim cmd/agent/route_provider_test.go and routeProvider-touching tests in routing_internal_test.go accordingly.
- Run: go test ./cmd/agent ./... -run "Test(BuildServiceExecuteRequest|CLI_ModelRoute|ExecuteEndpointFirstRouting|ResolveRoute|RouteStatus)" — must pass clean — then a broader `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` before committing.

2. **isExplicitPinError does NOT classify unknown provider as a rejected_override** (review-cited: service_execute.go:isExplicitPinError). AC #6 requires rejected_override on unknown provider; current implementation only fires on orphan-model. 3. **TestOverrideEventCoincidentalAgreement is fake** (review-cited: service_override_test.go:220). The test's own comment admits it does NOT synthesize a coincidental-agreement scenario — it asserts the event fires and that MatchPerAxis has entries, NOT that the entries are true. AC #3 is explicit: 'when pinning matches what unconstrained auto would produce, match_per_axis values are true; the event still fires.' Replace with a real synthesis: build a fakeServiceConfig with a single provider that auto-routing would pick anyway (e.g. only configured local provider with no other candidates), pin Provider=that-provider, assert match_per_axis[provider]=true and the event still fires. Routing-test-rigor memory applies — no synthetic stand-ins.

4. **TestExecuteEmitsOverrideEventBeforeFinal omits provider-only and model-only cases** (review-cited: service_override_test.go:134). AC #2 requires 'each axis individually and in combination.' The test covers harness-only, harness+model, and all three but skips provider-only and model-only. Add those subtests. Current preset names (prompt/presets.go, exposed via cmd/ddx-agent main.go --preset flag) are:
  agent | benchmark | claude | codex | cursor | minimal

Five of six are named after OTHER harnesses or products (claude, codex, cursor) or internal labels (agent, minimal). This creates real cognitive-load bugs in practice:

- 'preset codex' on the embedded 'agent' harness is semantically contradictory. 'codex' is a HARNESS (OpenAI's Codex CLI). Using it as a preset name on the ddx-agent invocation implies 'use the embedded agent but pretend to be codex' — why not just use the codex harness directly? The preset name should name an INTENT, not another implementation.

- Downstream config files like DocumentDrivenDX/ddx .ddx/config.yaml end up with lines like:

      harnesses:
        agent:
          binary: ./ddx-agent
          base_args: ['--json', '--preset', 'codex']

  A reader reasonably assumes this routes through codex. It doesn't. It runs the embedded ddx-agent with a prompt template styled in a 'codex-ish' way. Confusing and load-bearing wrong.

- Preset names encode prompt STYLE (instruction verbosity, tool description format, etc.), not provider choice. Calling that style 'codex' pins the meaning to whatever codex happens to do today; when codex changes, the preset either drifts or becomes misleadingly named.

## Proposed rename

Align preset vocabulary with DDx routing profile vocabulary (cheap | fast | smart) and add a 'default' for the middle. Explicit intent, no cross-reference to other tools.

  agent      -> default    (neutral prompt, balanced tool descriptions)
  benchmark  -> benchmark  (unchanged — evals use a named fixture, not a production preset)
  claude     -> smart      (the richest/most-verbose preset today; used when quality matters and tokens are cheap)
  codex      -> cheap      (the terse preset today; used when tokens/latency matter)
  cursor     -> (drop or merge into default) — 'cursor' is a specific IDE product, not a prompt-intent category
  minimal    -> minimal    (unchanged — legitimate style: smallest possible prompt, for latency-critical or low-context use)

Final name set: cheap | default | smart | minimal | benchmark (5, down from 6).

## Migration

1. Add the new names as first-class preset IDs; keep the old names as deprecated aliases that emit a stderr warning on resolution ('preset name 'codex' is deprecated; use 'cheap' — this warning will be fatal in vX.X.X'). Don't break downstream configs at first.

2. Update README.md, SD-003, and any other doc that references the old names.

3. After one release with deprecation warnings, remove the old names and upgrade the warning to an error.

4. DocumentDrivenDX/ddx will update its .ddx/config.yaml in a coordinated commit once new names ship.

## Other issues with preset names

- 'claude' as a preset name pins Claude-specific prompt conventions into a label that will be wrong if Claude's prompting conventions change. 'smart' is future-proof.
- Preset naming is exposed in session logs, bead execution evidence, and routing events. Confusing names poison those artifacts for anyone reading them later.

## Out of scope

- Changing what each preset actually DOES (tool description text, instruction style). Only the names.
- Adding new presets. The model itself is functional, our harness needs a lot of work.'

This bead is the iteration loop, not a one-shot benchmark.

## Methodology

**Backing.** omlx Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit on vidar (the local omlx host). NOT openrouter — the user's stated target is local omlx.

**Pi configuration.** Pi --list-models on the test machine doesn't currently include omlx. First step: ensure pi is configured to talk to omlx vidar (the user's target). This may require:
- Pi config file edit on the test machine (out of scope for direct manipulation per user directive 'just consume what pi tells us')
- OR a different test machine where pi already has omlx
- OR a pi command-line --provider flag that points at vidar

Capture the pi --list-models snapshot under the omlx-configured pi; that snapshot is the baseline evidence.

**Paired design.** Each task runs on BOTH harnesses with same model, same prompt:
- agent-omlx-vidar-qwen36 (harness=agent, provider=vidar-omlx, model=Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit)
- pi-omlx-vidar-qwen36 (harness=pi, provider=<pi-internal-omlx>, model=Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit)

**Reviewer pin.** Both arms use --review-harness codex --review-model gpt-5.5 (cannot be claude — confound).

**Sample size.** Minimum N=8 paired tasks; target N=12.

**Win condition.** Success rate ≥ pi's. Cost-per-success ≤ 1.2× pi's.

## Iteration loop (the actual work)

The baseline measurement is step zero. After it lands:

1. **Identify top-1 gap** — which lever moved the needle most against agent? Compaction policy, tool exposure, system prompt, or reasoning encoding?
2. **Tweak that lever** — file a small focused bead (e.g., 'compaction: tune Qwen-friendly summary trigger') and implement.
3. **Re-measure** — append a new dated parity row to the tracker (agent-f43d1ed2).
4. **Repeat** until agent matches or beats pi for 3 consecutive measurements.

The iteration beads are filed reactively as data surfaces, not upfront.

## Levers (per user signal)

- **Compaction.** internal/compaction/. May be too aggressive or too lax for Qwen's smaller context strategies.
- **Tools.** internal/tool/. Tool descriptions, parallelism, tool count. Qwen may be confused by tool sets that work fine for Claude/GPT.
- **System prompt.** internal/prompt/presets.go. Default and benchmark presets may be tuned for stronger models.
- **Reasoning levels.** Reasoning encoding through openai-compat to omlx. Qwen3.6 is a thinking-variant model; we may be sending the wrong wire shape.

## What is blocking

AC #2 ("Pi configuration verified: pi --list-models snapshot shows omlx is in
pi's reachable provider set") is **not satisfiable in this environment**. The
bead description anticipates this exact situation and lists three possible
unblockers:

          "just consume what pi tells us"

        — execute-bead worktrees run on this Linux host; we cannot relocate

        — pi has no openai-compatible / generic-http provider; the four
          providers listed above are the only options. There is no
          `--provider vidar-omlx` or equivalent.

Because pi cannot be made to call vidar OMLX, no `pi-omlx-vidar-qwen36` arm
can be exercised, no paired runs (AC #3, N≥8 in AC #4) can be produced,
no aggregate metrics (AC #5) or top-3 gaps ranked from pairwise data
(AC #6) can be filed honestly. Filing a one-arm "comparison" would defeat
the bead's purpose (driving the next iteration tweak from gap evidence).

A secondary blocker exists for the reviewer pin: `gpt-5.5` does not exist
in pi's catalog. Even if pi gained omlx, the manifest entry would have to
be reframed — likely against `gpt-5.4` (current codex top) or against the
codex CLI directly.

   Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit`). Once `pi --list-models` (or a
   `--provider openai-compat` invocation) can reach vidar, AC #2 becomes
   satisfiable and the paired runs become possible.

   This likely requires either (a) a pi version bump that adds
   openai-compatible support, or (b) a pi config-file edit registering
   vidar as a custom provider — the latter is explicitly out of scope per
   the user directive cited in the bead.

2. **OR the bead is reframed** to compare the agent's vidar OMLX arm
   against pi's nearest-available qwen3.6 (openrouter
   `qwen/qwen3.6-plus`). That changes the comparison from "same model,
   different harness" to "different model + different harness", which
   confounds the iteration signal the bead wants. Worth flagging to the
   user, but a reframe — not the work this bead asked for.

`HarnessEntry` in `internal/routing/engine.go` has no field for the harness's supported-models allow-list. `internal/routing/gating.go:88` checks only `ExactPinSupport` when validating a model pin. `engine.go:456` `resolveModel` returns `req.Model` directly when no provider discovery is present. Result: any harness with `ExactPinSupport: true` and `Available: true` is eligible for **any** model, regardless of the allow-list declared in `internal/harnesses/registry.go`.

Concrete failure observed on a DDx consumer (2026-04-22): `ResolveRoute(Profile: "default", Model: "minimax/minimax-m2.7")` returned `harness: gemini` on a machine where gemini CLI was installed. Gemini's registry declares `Models: [gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite]` — explicitly excluding minimax. The engine ignored the allow-list because it never reached the routing layer. DDx consumer then invoked the gemini CLI with the minimax model; CLI rejected it; escalation retried 19 times; 19 bead claims burned.

## Scope

1. Extend `HarnessEntry` in `internal/routing/engine.go` with a `SupportedModels []string` field (nil = no allow-list / rely on provider-side validation).
2. Populate `SupportedModels` in `service_routing.go`'s `buildRoutingInputs` from each harness's `cfg.Models`.
3. In `internal/routing/gating.go`, add a gate: when `h.SupportedModels != nil` AND `req.Model != ""` AND `req.Model ∉ h.SupportedModels`, mark candidate ineligible with reason `"model not in harness allow-list"`. This gate applies **regardless** of `ExactPinSupport` — `ExactPinSupport: true` means "accepts exact pins within its allow-list," not "accepts anything."
4. For harnesses with `SupportedModels: nil` (e.g., any that genuinely proxy to any provider), behavior unchanged — rely on provider-side validation.
5. Fuzzy matching against provider's `DiscoveredIDs` continues to take precedence when the harness has a provider entry with live discovery.

## Regression test

Seed a routing.Inputs with:
- `gemini` harness, Available=true, ExactPinSupport=true, SupportedModels=[gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite]
- `agent` harness with a live endpoint whose DiscoveredIDs contains `minimax/minimax-m2.7`

`Resolve(Request{Profile: "default", Model: "minimax/minimax-m2.7"}, inputs)` must return `Decision{Harness: "agent", ...}`. Must **never** return gemini. Remove the `agent` entry and assert the engine returns `no viable candidate` typed error, not a gemini pick.

DDx keeps a process-local provider-health shadow (`cli/internal/escalation/GlobalProviderHealth`) because the Service contract has no public way for a consumer to tell the service "this resolved candidate just failed; please don't hand it back in the next 30 seconds."

The execute-loop needs to know: after a ResolveRoute winner fails with a transient error (provider timeout, stream crash, 502, rate-limit), the NEXT ResolveRoute call within a cooldown window should demote or skip that candidate. Without an upstream feedback path, DDx shadow-tracks it, then has to either re-resolve from scratch or use its own ad-hoc cooldown.

Agent already owns route scoring, quota, and subscription-burn influence. Adding a feedback channel slots cleanly in.

## Proposal

Expose a deterministic feedback method, e.g.:

- Service.RecordRouteAttempt(ctx, RouteAttempt{Harness, Provider, Model, Endpoint, Status, Error, DurationMs}) error

Or event-driven: ServiceEvent of Kind="route-attempt" emitted by Execute can be mirrored by consumers back to Service.ReportRouteFailure for manually-dispatched calls.

Behavior: future ResolveRoute / RouteStatus in the same process (or same persistent state scope) demotes or skips candidates with active failures. Failure records expire on a TTL. RouteStatus reports them.

## Consumer impact

Status: not attempted in this pass; bead should be split into smaller follow-ups before another execution attempt.

## What is already in place from step 1 (agent-ddcc903b)

Plumbing for the public auto-selection inputs is already done at HEAD (fa6a5d7):

- service_routing.go:49-50 — req.EstimatedPromptTokens and req.RequiresTools are already passed into routing.Request when ResolveRoute builds the engine input.
- internal/routing/engine.go:25-30 — routing.Request already carries those fields.
- internal/routing/gating.go:85-93 — CheckGating already enforces context-window and tools gates against the engine's Capabilities struct (cap.ContextWindow / cap.SupportsTools).
- service_route_attempts.go + service.go:602-607 — routeAttemptKey is already keyed by (Harness, Provider, Model, Endpoint), and routeMetricSignals already emits per-(provider,model) signals via routing.ProviderModelKey at service_route_attempts.go:184. There is no per-tier adaptive min-tier window in the current code to delete — the adaptive lockout described in ADR-005 §"Two adjacent observed behaviors" appears to already have been removed in earlier work.
- internal/routing/engine.go:803-831 — EscalateProfileAware exists as a helper but is not currently called by service_routing.go.

## What this bead still requires (and why each is its own non-trivial piece of work)

1. **End-to-end gate firing** (AC #1). The engine's ContextWindow gate fires only when ProviderEntry.ContextWindows[model] is populated. service.buildRoutingInputsWithCatalog never sets that map today (grep ContextWindows --include='*.go' has zero hits in service_routing.go and zero in liveProviderEntries). Wiring this means populating ContextWindows from modelcatalog.Catalog.ContextWindowForModel for every DiscoveredID and the DefaultModel on each ProviderEntry, plus a public-package test using a real ServiceConfig fixture that exercises the gate.

2. **Liveness escalation in ResolveRoute** (AC #2). Requires:
   - Introducing a profile→tier ladder (code-economy → code-medium → code-high → smart), either from the catalog manifest's targets or hard-coded.
   - Detecting the empty-after-filter condition in service_routing.go.ResolveRoute (the engine returns NoViableCandidateError today; need to inspect this and re-call with the next ladder profile).
   - Replacing the engine's "no viable routing candidate: N candidates rejected" jargon with the bead's required precise error: "no live provider supports prompt of N tokens with tools=B at tier ≥ X".
   - This is non-trivial because the public publicRoutingError mapping in service_routing.go:161 must learn to translate this new internal error type, and the existing TestResolveRoute_* tests must still pass.

3. **Per-(provider,model) keying test** (AC #3). The keying is structurally correct already; this is the smallest piece (a focused test asserting that recording three failures on (provider=A, model=X) does not change the success-rate signal observed for (provider=A, model=Y)).

4. **route-status full redesign** (AC #4). cmd/agent/routing_smart.go:750 cmdRouteStatus today goes through buildSmartRoutePlan over agentConfig.ModelRouteConfig — a parallel implementation distinct from service.ResolveRoute. The bead asks to:
   - Drop the model_routes enumeration entirely.
   - Construct a *service via agent.New(...) inside the CLI path (today only executeViaService at cmd/agent/main.go:301 does this).
   - Call svc.ResolveRoute with --profile / --model-ref flags.
   - Render the full ranked candidate list with per-axis component scores + filter_reason.
   - Update TestCLI_RouteStatusShowsHealthAndScoringForModelIntent at cmd/agent/routing_cli_test.go:480 (which currently expects the legacy route_key/selected_provider JSON shape) and add the new TestRouteStatus_ShowsEligibleCandidatesPerIntent.
   This is a CLI restructuring on the order of 200-300 LOC plus new tests, and it changes the externally visible JSON shape of route-status.

5. **Test rigor (feedback memory: feedback_routing_test_rigor)**. The acceptance criteria explicitly demand strategy coverage, ordering assertions (not just set membership), structural boundary tests, and real ServiceConfig fixtures rather than synthetic mocks for the integration tests. Each of items 1, 2, and 4 above needs its own carefully built fixture catalog (loadRoutingFixtureCatalog) + ServiceConfig pair to exercise the escalation/gate/health paths deterministically.

## Why I am stopping rather than committing partial work

A bead-d9c358ba scoped to this much surface (engine wiring + service-level escalation + signal redesign + CLI redesign + four new test files with prescribed names and rigor expectations) is at least three follow-up beads' worth of work. Each piece has a non-trivial fan-out (e.g., escalation requires changes in publicRoutingError, possibly internal/routing/engine.go's error type, and updates to multiple existing tests; route-status redesign rewrites an existing CLI command and breaks existing test assertions). Trying to land all of this in one pass risks committing red tests or, worse, half-applied behavior changes that mask the real ADR-005 step 2 surface.

## What is already in place from step 1 (agent-ddcc903b)

Plumbing for the public auto-selection inputs is already done at HEAD (fa6a5d7):

- service_routing.go:49-50 — req.EstimatedPromptTokens and req.RequiresTools are already passed into routing.Request when ResolveRoute builds the engine input.

## What this bead still requires (and why each is its own non-trivial piece of work)

1. **End-to-end gate firing** (AC #1). The engine's ContextWindow gate fires only when ProviderEntry.ContextWindows[model] is populated. service.buildRoutingInputsWithCatalog never sets that map today (grep ContextWindows --include='*.go' has zero hits in service_routing.go and zero in liveProviderEntries). Wiring this means populating ContextWindows from modelcatalog.Catalog.ContextWindowForModel for every DiscoveredID and the DefaultModel on each ProviderEntry, plus a public-package test using a real ServiceConfig fixture that exercises the gate.

2. **Liveness escalation in ResolveRoute** (AC #2). Requires:
   - Introducing a profile→tier ladder (code-economy → code-medium → code-high → smart), either from the catalog manifest's targets or hard-coded.
   - Detecting the empty-after-filter condition in service_routing.go.ResolveRoute (the engine returns NoViableCandidateError today; need to inspect this and re-call with the next ladder profile).
   - Replacing the engine's "no viable routing candidate: N candidates rejected" jargon with the bead's required precise error: "no live provider supports prompt of N tokens with tools=B at tier ≥ X".
   - This is non-trivial because the public publicRoutingError mapping in service_routing.go:161 must learn to translate this new internal error type, and the existing TestResolveRoute_* tests must still pass.

3. **Per-(provider,model) keying test** (AC #3). The keying is structurally correct already; this is the smallest piece (a focused test asserting that recording three failures on (provider=A, model=X) does not change the success-rate signal observed for (provider=A, model=Y)).

   - Drop the model_routes enumeration entirely.
   - Construct a *service via agent.New(...) inside the CLI path (today only executeViaService at cmd/agent/main.go:301 does this).
   - Call svc.ResolveRoute with --profile / --model-ref flags.
   - Render the full ranked candidate list with per-axis component scores + filter_reason.
   - Update TestCLI_RouteStatusShowsHealthAndScoringForModelIntent at cmd/agent/routing_cli_test.go:480 (which currently expects the legacy route_key/selected_provider JSON shape) and add the new TestRouteStatus_ShowsEligibleCandidatesPerIntent.
   This is a CLI restructuring on the order of 200-300 LOC plus new tests, and it changes the externally visible JSON shape of route-status.

5. **Test rigor (feedback memory: feedback_routing_test_rigor)**. The acceptance criteria explicitly demand strategy coverage, ordering assertions (not just set membership), structural boundary tests, and real ServiceConfig fixtures rather than synthetic mocks for the integration tests. Each of items 1, 2, and 4 above needs its own carefully built fixture catalog (loadRoutingFixtureCatalog) + ServiceConfig pair to exercise the escalation/gate/health paths deterministically.

Each piece has a non-trivial fan-out (e.g., escalation requires changes in publicRoutingError, possibly internal/routing/engine.go's error type, and updates to multiple existing tests; route-status redesign rewrites an existing CLI command and breaks existing test assertions). After agent-04639431 landed in v0.3.13 (stripped 'thinking' field for non-Anthropic flavors), 'ddx work --provider vidar-omlx' still fails with 'unexpected end of JSON input' in the same symptom shape. The v0.3.13 fix is correct — wire capture confirms 'thinking' is no longer in the request body — but the root cause of the parse failure is deeper.

## Tightened wire evidence

Captured 2026-04-18 on v0.3.13 via AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE=1:

Request body (33,426 bytes, top-level keys: messages, model, stream, stream_options, tools):
- model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit
- stream: true
- stream_options: {include_usage: true}
- NO 'thinking' field (v0.3.13 strip working)
- NO 'system' top-level (uses messages[].role=system)
- 7 tools with valid JSON Schema shapes

Response (captured by AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE):
- HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
- Body captured: 186 bytes
  - : keep-alive\n\n
  - data: {...choices:[{delta:{role:"assistant"}}]}\n\n
- Then AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE capture stops; SDK parser surfaces 'unexpected end of JSON input'

## The key finding: same body works via curl

Piping the exact same 33,426-byte request body via curl to the same endpoint returns a valid, continuously-streaming SSE response:

    curl -sS -N -X POST http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -H 'Accept: application/json' \
      -d @req.json

    → role delta → reasoning_content stream → (continues generating)

The server takes ~9 seconds between 'role:assistant' frame and first 'reasoning_content' frame (model warmup). During this silence the server emits ': keep-alive' SSE comment frames periodically.

So the wire-level body is fine. The server is fine. The difference is entirely in how the openai-go SDK (wrapped by ddx-agent) consumes the stream.

## Suspected root causes (ranked)

1. **The 9-second reasoning-warmup silence exceeds an openai-go client-side idle/read timeout.** The SDK may be closing or aborting the underlying HTTP connection during the server's reasoning phase, before generation tokens arrive. ': keep-alive' SSE comment frames are supposed to prevent this — the SDK may not be resetting its idle timer on comment frames.

2. **HTTP/2 connection negotiation differs from curl's HTTP/1.1 default.** omlx server (uvicorn per response headers) may serve SSE differently under HTTP/2 multiplexing vs HTTP/1.1. openai-go client likely enables HTTP/2 by default.

3. **Buffer/goroutine interaction in the SDK's streaming decoder.** The decoder's internal buffering may drop frames under specific arrival-time patterns (long silence, then burst).

4. **AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE may be misleading.** The 186-byte response capture may represent only the first response batch read by the debug middleware, with subsequent frames going to the SDK parser unobserved. If so, the parse failure occurs later in the stream, not at the 186-byte point. Either way, the result is the same: the SDK parser surfaces 'unexpected end of JSON input' when curl against the same server does not.

## Reproduction

- Host: eitri, DDx binary v0.6.0-alpha22-15 (commit 9d87594b, agent-lib v0.3.13)
- Provider: vidar-omlx (http://vidar:1235/v1)
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit (a reasoning model — 9s warmup is typical)
- Command: ddx work --once --local --provider vidar-omlx --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit --max-tier cheap

Wire evidence: /tmp/vidar-omlx-wire2.jsonl on eitri.

## Suggested investigation steps

1. Add a packet-level capture (tcpdump on port 1235) during a failing ddx-agent run AND a working curl run with identical body, compare.

2. Instrument openai-go client transport to log HTTP connection-level events (idle timeout, connection close, context cancel).

3. Test with an explicit http.Transport that disables HTTP/2 (ForceAttemptHTTP2: false) and see if that changes behavior.

4. Test with an artificially slow reasoning phase on a simpler omlx model to reproduce the silence-triggered cutoff deterministically.

5. Extend AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE to capture the ENTIRE stream (not just the first batch) so the exact client-side truncation point is visible in the evidence bundle.

- agent-941e7e42 (v0.3.12): AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE — needs extension per step 5 above.

- claude-code harness (gpt-oss-20b via openrouter): 1 attempt, same failure

### Common failure pattern (all fiz.txt logs)
```
{
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "agent: provider error: Post \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority",
  "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "total": 0 }
}
```

### Root cause hypothesis
The overfull-hbox Docker container environment does not have the required CA certificates to verify the OpenRouter TLS certificate. All calls to openrouter.ai fail immediately with x509 certificate verification error. This is a harness environment issue, not a model capability issue. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (2026-05-03):
Harbor task Docker Compose networks use isolated bridge DNS that does NOT
inherit the host's Tailscale DNS. When fiz inside the task container tries
to connect to http://bragi:1234/v1, DNS resolution for 'bragi' fails with
"Could not resolve host". This causes fiz to hang at the first API call and
produce 0 output until harbor's agent timeout kills the process.

The same issue affects vidar (http://vidar:1235/v1) — confirmed via docker
network tests on named Compose networks. Earlier vidar runs only worked
because the default Docker bridge network WAS used (before isolating into
named per-task networks, or via a different docker run invocation).

Additional complexity with bragi/LMStudio: even accessing by Tailscale IP
(100.127.38.115) fails because LMStudio uses Host-header routing and returns
404 when the Host header is an IP address instead of the hostname 'bragi'.

FIX: harbor_agent.py now resolves FIZEAU_BASE_URL hostname on the host
(where Tailscale DNS works) during container install and injects the
{hostname → ip} mapping into /etc/hosts. This provides both DNS resolution
AND correct Host header in HTTP requests.

Fix committed: 69eb184 "fix: inject FIZEAU_BASE_URL hostname into /etc/hosts
for harbor task containers"

- **Power** — an integer model-strength score from 1 to 10. Higher means more
  capable for agent tasks. `0` means unknown, missing, or not eligible for
  automatic routing.
- **Provider/deployment class** — catalog provenance describing whether a model
  is a managed cloud frontier model, prepaid harness model, metered API model,
  local/free inference server, community/self-hosted copy, or test model.
  Benchmarks alone do not make different deployment classes equivalent.
- **Route candidate** — one discovered `(harness, provider source, endpoint,
  model)` option after joining live inventory with catalog metadata
- **Server instance** — the concrete inference server reached by a candidate,
  derived from endpoint configuration or normalized host/port, such as
  `grendel`, `vidar`, or `sindri`. Stickiness targets server instances, not
  model strings.
- **Sticky route key** — a request sequence identity, normally the validated
  `CorrelationID` or a future worker/session sequence ID, used to bias related
  requests toward the same server instance
- **Endpoint utilization** — a normalized operational signal for one provider
  endpoint, including active requests, queued/deferred requests, concurrency
  when known, cache pressure when known, freshness, and source
- **Prompt preset** — system prompt selection (`preset`, `--preset`); unrelated
  to model policy and routing

28. Automatic routing excludes inactive, deprecated, exact-pin-only, and
    unknown-power models unless the caller explicitly pins that model and live
    discovery confirms it is available.
29. The router ranks survivors by model power, provider/deployment placement,
    effective marginal cost, prepaid quota, availability, maximum configured
    context length, context/capability fit, observed speed/latency, normalized
    utilization, and sticky server-instance affinity.
30. When unpinned local/free LLMs are available and satisfy requested power,
    tools, context, and health constraints, they are preferred over paid cloud
    candidates. This local/free preference never overrides hard pins,
    `MinPower`/`MaxPower`, or capability requirements.
30a. For multiple eligible local/free server instances, routing assigns each
     new sticky route key to the least-loaded eligible server instance. Load
     combines service-owned in-flight route leases with fresh provider-owned
     utilization probes when available. Requests with the same sticky route key
     receive a ranking bonus for that server instance so worker-local cache
     behavior stays stable across related requests, including requests that use
     a different model on the same server.
30b. Sticky affinity never bypasses eligibility. A sticky server instance may
     lose when it no longer satisfies hard pins, power policy, context,
     capability, health, quota, or hard saturation constraints. A merely better
     score on another server instance is not enough to move an existing sticky
     key; severe utilization or performance pressure is enough when the scoring
     policy says the affinity bonus is outweighed.
30c. On a single machine, in-process route leases provide the authoritative
     sticky assignment and fallback load count. On multiple machines, correct
     cross-process stickiness and fair distribution require a shared lease
     backend; server metrics are advisory and racy, not a replacement for
     shared leases. See

The focused run is now specific: `RouteStatus` test needs a seeded server identity in its fixture, and the session-log path isn’t yet projecting `RoutingActual.ServerInstance` into the emitted JSON. I’m checking the log writer and the routing-status builder to wire those through instead of weakening the acceptance.

I’ve got a concrete fix path now: normalize the server identity when `RouteStatus` builds candidates, and let the session log prefer the resolved `RoutingActual.server_instance` when the pre-resolved decision doesn’t carry one. I’m checking the existing config tests so I can keep the test additions aligned with the grendel/vidar/sindri cases already in the tree.

- normalize `RouteStatus` candidates from `BaseURL` when a config fixture doesn’t pre-fill `server_instance`
- let `session.end` prefer the runtime `RoutingActual.server_instance` as a fallback
- seed the session-log test with an explicit route identity so it exercises the new field instead of an empty fixture.

The code changes are in. I’m formatting and rerunning the focused acceptance slice plus the two root-package tests I touched so I can verify the fix without pulling in the unrelated Gemini-profile regression.
